title: Seller Soundboard: Rapid Labs & Variant Cards (draft)
body:
Goal: build a compact, variant-first enablement pack sellers can carry into a pilot or discovery call. Think pocket-lab: 6 slides + 8 micro-battlecards + 3 pilot scripts, each with fast metrics and a single visual cue to anchor the conversation.

Status: rough collection of slide titles, speaker bullets, micro-battlecards and quick scripts. This is intentionally modular — we want small cards that can be swapped in based on buyer persona (platform engineer, integration architect, product manager).

Audience notes
- Primary: SEs and platform sellers (30–60 min prep before call).
- Secondary: SDRs prepping for technical discovery (1–2 talking points).
- Use when: pilot conversation, reserved capacity negotiation, migration-to-dedicated decisioning.

Deck skeleton (6 slides; each slide should be 6–12 words max + 2 speaker bullets)
1) Title: "Pilot Fast: Predictable Inference Without Reinventing Ops"
   - Speaker notes: 30s opener: cost + latency are the gate. Show one line: "Same API. Pick hosted, dedicated, or private."
   - Visual cue: three stacked icons (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) with a green tick on "same API"

2) Title: "Where projects stall: top 3 operator friction points"
   - Bullet friction points: unpredictable tail latency; cost spikes from naive batching; rollout/regression risk on model swaps
   - Quick stat: "Customers see 2–5x token cost reduction after cache+batches applied" (callout: internal case INF-3421)

3) Title: "Redwood playbook: routing + cache + graceful fallbacks"
   - Speaker notes: show how smart routing + KV/prefix caching reduces cost and preserves SLOs; mention automatic fallbacks when capacity constrained
   - Callout: one-sentence example: "Route low-priority requests to quantized variants to save 40% unit cost"

4) Title: "Pilot plan (14 days): quick wins and check-ins"
   - 0–3 days: instrument routes + baseline tokens/latency
   - 4–9 days: enable prefixKV caching on hot routes; run A/B with cache on/off
   - 10–14 days: iterate quantization profile + validate quality on prompt set
   - Deliverable: pilot handoff doc + go/no-go checklist

5) Title: "Fallback & SLA choreography for enterprise buyers"
   - Show default fallback chain: Dedicated primary -> Hosted low-latency pool -> Quantized fallback -> Degraded feature with explanation header to user
   - Legal & compliance note (private deployments): KMS/HSM available; audit logs retained 90 days by default

6) Title: "Success metrics & handshake to procurement"
   - KPIs to track during pilot: p50/p95 latency; token/unit cost; percent requests served from cache; model regression rate on eval set
   - Closing ask: "Reserve a 2-week pilot with scoped SLAs and a demo integration task"

Mini-battlecards (single-page, single-sentence headline + 3 bullets + one quick rebuttal)
- Card: "Cost Shock: \"We can't afford token spikes\""
  - Bullet 1: show a micro-metric: "Autoscaled workloads without cache = unpredictable token cost spikes"
  - Bullet 2: Redwood lever: smart batching + prefix cache throttles token churn
  - Bullet 3: Quick ROI: "pilot often reveals 20–60% unit cost savings depending on prompt reuse"
  - Rebuttal script: "Let's sandbox your top 5 routes and I'll show cost delta within 72 hours"

- Card: "Latency Risk: \"LLMs are too slow for product\""
  - Bullet 1: p95 delivered matters more than p50 for UX
  - Bullet 2: Redwood offers routing by latency SLO and a dedicated pool option for predictable p95
  - Bullet 3: Technical ask: collect trace headers for 3 heavy endpoints; we can baseline in one day
  - Rebuttal: "If p95 is critical, we'll propose a dedicated pool with 99th percentile SLA and a fallback plan for bursts"

- Card: "Security: \"We need on-prem or VPC-only\""
  - Bullet 1: Redwood Private supports VPC + on-prem packages with optional air-gapped installs
  - Bullet 2: KMS/HSM integrations + per-customer audit logs
  - Bullet 3: Delivery note: Private takes longer; propose staged pilot via dedicated with contractual controls
  - Rebuttal: "We'll scope a dedicated pilot with contractual data isolation while Private packaging timelines are worked out"

Pilot scripts (3 variants)
1) Engineer-first: "Show me the latency and cost drops"
- 5-min plan: run baseline curl to /v1/generate for 3 endpoints; enable prefixKV caching; show p50/p95 before & after; discuss kernel/quantization options
- Quick artifact: attach a perf-run CSV + flame graph to the pilot handoff

2) Product PM: "Prove UX reliability and cost predictability"
- 5-min plan: show p95 reduction story + user-facing fallback text for degraded responses; discuss observable SLO dashboard and alert hooks
- Quick artifact: template SLA language + UX fallback copy (1–2 lines users will see)

3) Procurement/Finance: "Numbers and contract ask"
- 5-min plan: show projected monthly spend with & without caching/quantization; proposed reserved capacity commit tier; highlight add-ons: SLA, extended retention
- Quick artifact: one-pager TCO table (monthly run rate, savings from caching, break-even months)

Open questions (to resolve before next iter)
- Which pilot metrics page will be the canonical source of truth? (Confluence vs Console export)
- Need final legal template for 30-day pilot with reserved capacity conversion clause (talk to Legal: Nora Jensen)
- Do we include a worked example for embeddings-heavy workflows vs generative chat?

- Emma L: sketch 3 micro-battlecards for 'edge' and 'regulated' buyers — due 2025-11-14
- Aisha: consolidate pilot handoff template and ship to /sales-assets repo PR#87 — due 2025-11-18

Notes to self
- Keep cards <120 words each; sellers should be able to memorize 6 cards easily.
- Design ask: each card needs a single icon and a color band (cost=orange, latency=blue, security=grey)
- Risk: too many technical options will confuse procurement; always lead with a single recommended path and call out alternatives as bullets.
